summary: Feed s119_double to NDR is degraded: 2.3% TCP packet loss and 29.2% ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic reduce detection coverage. NDR will miss flow reassembly and fail to inspect inner payloads for nearly a third of traffic.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN path is dropping packets before the NDR (2.28% TCP gaps, 34/1493 packets) - classic buffer exhaustion/oversubscription on ingress or fabric, not tool overload (tool_overload healthy). Sequence gaps at frames 51/52, 71/72 etc indicate broker discards under burst.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions and full payload for flow reassembly and detection; missing segments break TCP stream reconstruction, cause false negatives, missed C2/exfiltration detection and incomplete Zeek/Suricata logs.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load across NDR pool / reduce per-tool throughput and broker egress congestion to eliminate 2%+ drops; also review SPAN oversubscription and consider TAP aggregation with load balancing.

findings.root_cause: 29.2% of frames (453/1554) arrive encapsulated in ERSPAN from remote source; packet broker is forwarding tunnel intact without stripping outer header before NDR handoff.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees outer ERSPAN/IP/GRE headers instead of inner Ethernet/IP payload; without decapsulation it cannot parse inner 5-tuple, application payload or VLANs, so ~29% of traffic is opaque to detection and analytics.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip ERSPAN and forward inner original frames to NDR so it can inspect L2-L7 and apply VLAN/policy detection on required VLANs 10,20.
